The formation operates under a deterministic kinematic model where each player contributes a directional vector to the overall play trajectory. The right half back's path is defined by the quarterback's toss and the alignment of the offensive line. The center's block initiates a force vector that propels the opposing center laterally. The left guard reinforces this by applying an additional impulse, creating a compound effect. The left tackle's breakthrough behind the line acts as a cut-off mechanism, while the right tackle blocks the opposing left guard. These actions form a closed-loop system where each role is a function of others' positioning and timing. Failure modes include misalignment of vectors, delayed execution, or defensive counterplay disrupting the intended motion. The system's robustness depends on synchronized movement and precise force application across all players.
